name: Communist Party of China (Chinese Soviet Republic, Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region and Liberated Areas)
native: 中华苏维埃共和国 (Zhōnghuá Sūwéi'āi Gònghéguó)

predecessors.name: Chinese Communists (Jinggangshan and Jiangxi soviet bases)
predecessors.text: the Jiangxi-Fujian soviet area of the predecessor row plus a 100 km circle at Ruijin (116.03 E, the capital), which lies outside Cliopatria's 1930-1931 shape (it ends at 115.28 E)

predecessors.name: Republic of China
predecessors.text: the other soviets the page names as territories of the Republic (Minzhegan, Xianggan, Xiang'egan, Honghu, Xiang'echuanqian, Eyuwan, Eyushan, Shaanxi-Gansu, Sichuan-Shaanxi, Hailufeng): Cliopatria's…

predecessors.name: Shanxi clique
predecessors.text: Shanxi: most of the province in 1948, Taiyuan and Datong on 24 April 1949 and after (Taiyuan campaign page)

successors.name: People's Republic of China
successors.text: the communist-held land at the proclamation of 1 October 1949: north and northeast China, Shandong, Henan, Shanxi, the lower Yangtze south to Nanjing

ledger.x: 7 November 1931: Mao Zedong and Zhu De proclaim the Chinese Soviet Republic, with its capital at Ruijin.
ledger.cpn: Chinese Communists (Jinggangshan and Jiangxi soviet bases)

ledger.x: 7 November 1931: the Republic is proclaimed over the scattered soviets.
1933: Chiang's fifth encirclement campaign opens against the Jiangxi Soviet.
October 1934: the Communists abandon Ruijin and the Long March begins.
10 November 1934: Ruijin falls and the fifth encirclement campaign ends.
10 November 1934: the Jiangxi Soviet is lost with Ruijin.
November 1934: the Eyuwan bases are lost.
By 1935: the southern soviets are gone.
March 1935: the Fourth Red Army leaves the Sichuan-Shaanxi base.
19 October 1935: Mao's army reaches northern Shaanxi and joins the local Soviet.
ledger.cp: Northern Shaanxi Soviet (Liu Zhidan, Gao Gang, Xu Haidong)

ledger.x: 1936: the Communist seat is Bao'an.
January 1937: the CCP headquarters is established in Yan'an.
22 September 1937: the Chinese Soviet Republic becomes the Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region under the Second United Front.
September 1937: the Red Army becomes the Eighth Route Army and fights in the Japanese rear.
Spring 1939: the Border Region takes the rich east around Suide.
1945: the Liberated Zone of 19 base areas.
10 October 1945: the fighting period of the Eighth Route Army against Japan ends on the page.
March 1946: the war for the Northeast begins.
March 1947: the Nationalists seize Yan'an.
March 1947: the leadership leaves Yan'an.
30 June 1947: the Communists cross the Yellow River into the Central Plains.
By October 1948: most of Shanxi is Communist.
Spring 1948: the Communists hold the Northeast outside the garrison cities (no month given).
April 1948: Luoyang falls.
24 September 1948: Jinan falls and Shandong passes to the Communists.
14 October 1948: Jinzhou falls in the Liaoshen campaign.
19 October 1948: Changchun surrenders.
1 November 1948: Shenyang falls and Manchuria is won.
1 November 1948: the fighting for the Northeast ends.
21 November 1948: the Pingjin campaign opens.
January 1949: Beiping and Tianjin pass to the Communists.
31 January 1949: the Pingjin campaign ends.
Early 1949: the Huaihai campaign secures east-central China.
Early 1949: the Central Plains fighting ends with the Huaihai victory ('late 1948 and early 1949').
21-23 April 1949: the Yangtze is crossed and Nanjing falls.
24 April 1949: Taiyuan is taken.
1 October 1949: Mao Zedong proclaims the People's Republic at Tiananmen Square.

wars.name: Fifth encirclement campaign against the Jiangxi Soviet
wars.outcome: Nationalist victory: Ruijin fell on 10 November 1934 (infobox) and the Communists broke out of Jiangxi in October.

wars.name: Long March
wars.outcome: The Communist armies left Jiangxi (October 1934), fought at the Xiang, Wu and Jinsha rivers and reached northern Shaanxi in October 1935; the First, Second and Fourth Armies met again in October 1936.

wars.name: Kuomintang attacks and blockade of the Shaan-Gan-Ning Border Region
wars.outcome: The Communists took the rich east including Suide in spring 1939; the KMT banned aid on 6 January 1941 and tried to encircle the region; a KMT attack was repelled in March 1941.

wars.name: Chinese Civil War
wars.outcome: Communist victory: the People's Republic was proclaimed on 1 October 1949 and the Nationalist government left for Taiwan on 7 December 1949.

wars.name: Liaoshen campaign
wars.outcome: Communist victory: Jinzhou (14 October), Changchun (19 October) and Shenyang (1 November) taken; Manchuria won.

wars.name: Pingjin campaign
wars.outcome: Communist victory: 'In January 1949, Beiping changed hands through a negotiated settlement.'

wars.name: Huaihai campaign
wars.outcome: Communist victory: it 'secured east-central China for the CCP'.

wars.name: Yangtze River Crossing campaign
wars.outcome: Communist victory: the crossing began on 21 April 1949 and Nanjing fell on 23 April.

certainty.note: Soviet districts held by guerrilla control, not by survey: the Jiangxi core is known by its capital, the other soviets by names without boundaries.
The Border Region and the 19 base areas of 1945 were rural districts behind Japanese lines; no boundary is on the pages.
Fronts moved campaign by campaign; only the cities (Yan'an, Luoyang, Jinzhou, Changchun, Shenyang, Beiping, Nanjing, Taiyuan) are dated.
